words: That you're illegal and they tell you "you have to do this because you're illegal, that's what they say.

speaker: CL
words: And well, better here, to go where people treat you badly in another place.

speaker: CL
words: Instead- I think that in Nevada they treat you less badly although if you find yourself-

speaker: CL
words: I have found myself like at work I have found people who have told me that for example: I worked in that carpentry workshop for years,

speaker: CL
words: I had spent about 14 years working there, when a person arrived there to work and according to what he said he knew how to

speaker: CL
words: work and that he knew how to work, but my boss said, "no, look, he doesn't know how to work," he told me,

speaker: CL
words: "Teach him like this, tell him how I want things to be done," and I remember that

speaker: CL
words: I told him, "Look, you have to do it like this" and he said to me, why? "Because Steve, who was the owner, likes things to be done like this-"

speaker: CL
words: Because he- his cabinets are of high quality and he charges a lot for them and he wants them to be well done"

speaker: CL
words: And this person tells me, "no, what do you know? if I have worked in this more than 30 years," and I thought he was upset because I was younger than him,

speaker: CL
words: But it turned out that he told me "No, I'm not going to let a Mexican come and teach me how to work" and I laughed.

speaker: CL
words: I said, "What, if I'm not teaching you, I'm telling you how things should be done here," and I remember that, yes.

speaker: CL
words: in conservation he told me that how was a Mexican going to teach him to work when I, rather, he has to teach me to speak English.

speaker: CL
words: I just laughed, I remember, but there is always someone who is going to tell you things that make you feel bad,

speaker: CL
words: and it happened to me two more times with different people but It didn't bother me anymore because I accepted my place, let's say,

speaker: CL
words: And it was better not to say anything. And I also had to behave because, as I said, I have always had two jobs.

speaker: CL
words: And if I work it is because I have five children and had many things to pay. So, it didn't even affect me that they said anything against me.

speaker: CL
words: Because I thought "well, if I always spend my time working in two jobs outside the house, to come here to fight or get involved in trouble,

speaker: CL
words: It is enough in my case working, why have problems with the police or even have immigration sent to me and take me away?

speaker: CL
words: I will be separated from the family or my children in this case; I never wanted to have or cause problems, or say anything.

speaker: CL
words: As I say, if one spends time working from one job to another, you are never at home, your children don't even look at you.

speaker: CL
words: Maybe they think that "my dad just spends his time outside, he's never here, he doesn't take me to McDonalds, he doesn't take me to Burger King,

speaker: CL
words: "None of that, until only on Sunday" and well, it is difficult not to be at home because you are working.

speaker: CL
words: And the children always wish that one was in their house, but I always preferred to work two jobs, although it was difficult not to be at home.

speaker: CL
words: Never, always busy, and if you go home, sometimes they are already asleep, when they are children they are asleep and when they are older.

speaker: CL
words: They are doing homework and you arrive late and then you give them a few minutes and then you're going to,

speaker: CL
words: I don't know maybe you're going to take a bath, eat or go to sleep and work the next day.

speaker: CL
words: Even on Saturdays I always worked both jobs, and for an undocumented person, losing a day of work is a lot, you have to work always every day you can.

speaker: CL
words: Because the date or the day that they tell you "You know what? You can no longer work because your social security number has flaws,"

speaker: CL
words: And they tell me that I have to fire you, because it always happens, they fire you because of your social security number that doesn't work.

speaker: CL
words: Is not valid to work and when one does not have documents, you have to work as you can, where you can and for as long as you can.

speaker: CL
words: Because when you're going to get to the date they are going to tell you there is no more work because your social says it is not valid for work.

speaker: CL
words: That's why you have to have two jobs and it can take two years, five years, ten years.

speaker: CL
words: And you keep working two jobs because you know that any day they are going to tell you "your job is over because your number doesn't work."

speaker: GS
words: Thank you very much for your comments about work. And since you're mentioning your family I would like to ask the question you said that

speaker: GS
words: you have had five children but can you tell me more about your family? How are they doing in school? What have they have done?

speaker: GS
words: And I must say, what has your family done that makes you very, very happy to be a dad?

speaker: CL
words: Well, the question was that-

speaker: GS
words: Can you tell me a little more about your five children and your family in general.

speaker: CL
words: Well, what can I say? I feel happy because, despite the fact that I have always been working two jobs,

speaker: CL
words: I always told my wife to stay at home, to tend to them or take care of them from the beginning, and now serve them.

speaker: CL
words: I feel very happy because everyone makes an effort to do well in school, and to be good in their courses and always be on top.

speaker: CL
words: in the way that they always have good rankings, they always worry about doing well in their classes, even trying to be, how can you say?

speaker: CL
words: One of best in school who are not behind and not- as close to the best as possible.

speaker: CL
words: And that they [children] finish high school and have the idea of going to university from the beginning.

speaker: CL
words: And that they are 100% convinced that they are going to enroll in the university.

speaker: CL
words: And that they are going to have a career and that makes me feel happy and content, sure that everything is going to be fine.

speaker: CL
words: Because, I see them, they are focused and confident, believing in what they are going to do, I think that's what makes me feel the most happy, happy, safe.

speaker: CL
words: Sure because if they manage to make their careers, they will do well, they will be able to raise a good family also.

speaker: CL
words: And be, I don't know, I don't want to say with economic solvency, but they are going to be better than me, with a lot of difference.

speaker: GS
words: So you do have children who are going to college or have graduated from college?

speaker: CL
words: Yes, the first one, who is already 24 years old, he graduated two years, and he works; I see that he is doing very well, he lives well.

speaker: CL
words: And also, well, I have two more who are in college and very convinced that they are going to finish their degrees.

speaker: CL
words: And well, I am going to be here to help them, and to, as you say, feel happier that something like this is achieved, it would be something very spectacular for me.

speaker: GS
words: Well, I congratulate you, and how did you learn how to manage money well? Because since have college students you had to manage your money

speaker: GS
words: well so that they could go to school and for them to have a way to go.

speaker: CL
words: Well I learned because, as I said from the beginning, when you are undocumented you always have to be prepared by saving money.

speaker: CL
words: Trying to always have something extra for what is going to happen, because we know that something, as an illegal, is going to happen to us.

speaker: CL
words: That suddenly you are out of work, or I know that immigration takes you, one is always with that fear.

speaker: CL
words: So, you learn to take care of your money, to save a little, try to save and since you have something now.

speaker: CL
words: If you have children who go to school, you have something to give them, what they ask of you for school.

speaker: GS
words: And another question I have for you is that this sounds like a success story. what many immigrants dream of when they come to the US,

speaker: GS
words: that their children manage to have a solid education, would you say this is one of your greatest achievements after living in the US?

speaker: CL
words: Yes, of course. For me, one of the greatest achievements- I think that the greatest or best achievement is that my children finish a university degree.

speaker: CL
words: Because that lasts longer and you keep it forever.

speaker: CL
words: Because, even I have bought myself a house to live in and I don't feel like it's something big compared to your children finishing a college degree.

speaker: GS
words: Thank you very much for answering my questions, and now I want to ask you one more question- Now you can you tell me some

speaker: GS
words: other topics that I have not mentioned that you would like to comment or talk about.

speaker: CL
words: Yes, I would like to comment on the same thing about- Well I don't know, many people here think that all undocumented people receive benefits

speaker: CL
words: from the government and all that, and I would like to say, or clarify because I have friends or yes I am going to say

speaker: CL
words: friends because I have known them for many years, people here, citizens here from Carson, that they always said comments that all Latinos, they said,

speaker: CL
words: "Mexicans receive support from the government, they live off the government," and I always told them- until one day I made it clear to them

speaker: CL
words: That being illegal, you can't even open a bank account, or much less have a loan like for a mortgage, for a house, or for a car.

speaker: CL
words: Get a car from an agency you can not. For example, many people think that one receives benefits such as government aid, either as money or I don't know.

speaker: CL
words: You won't even be able to receive medical service, nothing like that, nothing.

speaker: CL
words: And I don't know I would like to say more things but they don't come to mind.

speaker: GS
words: And you told me a while ago that you also paid taxes.

speaker: CL
words: Oh yeah and all that stuff. For example, many people believe that we do not pay taxes; we do have to do our income tax.

speaker: CL
words: And aside from that, when you do your income tax we have to pay fines for not having a social security number.

speaker: CL
words: You have to pay a fine, if you put your wife and she doesn't have a social either, you have to pay a double fine.

speaker: CL
words: And instead of sending you back, let's say money because you have citizen children they cut it off... they cut a lot of money off you.

speaker: CL
words: And the money they just give you what is supposedly the son's credit is supposed to be, 500 and 500 and that's it.

speaker: CL
words: So that's not any support they give you. How about that?

speaker: GS
words: Thank you very much for your answer and another question that I wanted to ask you is, Now that what you have mentioned about what you have experienced,

speaker: GS
words: what would you like to say to the politicians of our state and country or those who are involved in politics, like our senators,

speaker: GS
words: our representatives who need to know about the undocumented?

speaker: CL
words: I imagine that they already know, they already know, but they always play with people's feelings because I have memories since before 2000.

speaker: CL
words: Long before that, we are going to say.

speaker: CL
words: The parties fight among themselves that "I am going to help undocumented people" and "no, I'm going to help them" and "no me," and no one does.

speaker: CL
words: All they do is make you believe that they will help you for you to vote and they win.

speaker: CL
words: They make no effort to really verify who they can help or who they can benefit from, how can you say?

speaker: CL
words: With a reform or some way, that someone can fix your immigration papers, that is, having a card or a Green Card as it is called.

speaker: CL
words: I say they don't do it because they don't want to because, let's say, speaking in my case.

speaker: CL
words: If I have been here for more than 20 years, and I have always paid taxes, I have always been working in the same place and all that.

speaker: CL
words: I pay taxes for property tax and all that, they don't think they can verify a person, their criminal record, all that, anything and say.

speaker: CL
words: "Well you do qualify, you don't." But what do they do? Instead they talk in the television, speaking everything in general.

speaker: CL
words: So that everyone gets into a ruckus and at the end nothing happens. What I would say is that they should change laws a little more gently.

speaker: CL
words: That they say "okay, you bring me your application, tell me how you have behaved and I will tell you whether it is accepted or not, I accept you in this country."

speaker: CL
words: I imagine that would be very simple.

speaker: CL
words: All the people after verifying that they works and pay taxes or have a reason to be here, or is doing things right, why not give them an opportunity? But no.

speaker: CL
words: They prefer to talk to television and say I'm going to give papers to everyone and pure lies. How about that?

speaker: GS
words: Thank you very much for your answer and yes, politics is very, very difficult and has caused a lot of problems here in this country but,

speaker: GS
words: what would you like to say to other undocumented people or even people who are listening to your interview right now?

speaker: GS
words: What would you like to say to all those people?

speaker: CL
words: Well, I would like to tell all undocumented people like me to not get discouraged, time passes and time passes, five years pass, ten years, or even 20.

speaker: CL
words: Or more like me; At first I felt like something was missing, why didn't it happen? Why isn't the date coming?

speaker: CL
words: Well yes, I would like to tell everyone the other undocumented people to not worry about having that famous Green Card or that famous social security number.

speaker: CL
words: Better yet care about working well, be well in them with all citizens, not get in trouble with the police, and, I do not say wait.

speaker: CL
words: But from dedicating themselves to their children if they have children.

speaker: CL
words: To dedicating themselves to having children who can dedicate themselves to having children who can serve the community here.

speaker: CL
words: Who are good children, raise good children so that further ahead it is better and Carson City is better.

speaker: CL
words: And yes one gets old, and you can never have your papers.

speaker: CL
words: It doesn't matter, the important thing is that you left some good children, good citizens and Carson City is going to be better.

speaker: CL
words: And those children that you are leaving they're going to make maybe the government think better.

speaker: CL
words: And know that there is nothing wrong in raising the undocumented.

speaker: CL
words: Because if an undocumented person raises good citizens, it means that the father was also good, but he was not given the opportunity.

speaker: CL
words: It's the only way to be able maybe manifesting would be, but I do not say manifesting rather, dedicate yourself to raising good children.

speaker: GS
words: What would you like to say to all the people who are listening to your interview?

speaker: CL
words: Well, I don't know, I would like to say that- I don't have anything in mind but I would say that I wanted to talk, answer the questions because,

speaker: CL
words: As an undocumented person, you are always silent, in silence, you never say anything because you can't say anything.

speaker: CL
words: Who are we going to tell? if you, your vote is not useful for politics or for anything, nor your comment, nobody will listen to you.

speaker: CL
words: Why? Because you don't have a voice because you don't have a social security number.

speaker: CL
words: But, I would like to say that, I don't know, the most important thing would be for everyone to try to do the best they can.

speaker: GS
words: Thank you very much for answering my questions and this will be useful to many people and many students and to the University of Reno.
